concept_mcqs.stem:
Your layout contains 12 RGB photos tagged sRGB, several CMYK vector elements, and two Pantone spot inks for a dieline and a brand spot. The printer requires PDF/X-1a with output intent FOGRA39 (ISO Coated v2). Choose the Output settings that will convert only the RGB to the destination CMYK, preserve existing CMYK numbers, and keep spot inks as spot plates.

Current export preset excerpt:
```text
Standard: PDF/X-1a:2001
Output:
  Color Conversion: [choose]
  Destination: [choose]
  Include Destination Profile: [auto per PDF/X-1a]
  Ink Manager: All Spots to Process = OFF
```
options:
```text
Color Conversion: No Color Conversion
Destination: Document CMYK
Include Destination Profile: OFF
```

```text
Color Conversion: Convert to Destination
Destination: ISO Coated v2 (ECI) [FOGRA39]
Include Destination Profile: OFF
```

```text
Color Conversion: Convert to Destination (Preserve Numbers)
Destination: ISO Coated v2 (ECI) [FOGRA39]
Include Destination Profile: OFF (Output Intent only)
```

```text
Color Conversion: Convert to Destination (Preserve Numbers)
Destination: sRGB IEC61966-2.1
Include Destination Profile: ON
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: PDF/X-1a requires a CMYK+spot workflow. Convert to Destination (Preserve Numbers) converts tagged RGB to the destination while leaving existing CMYK values unchanged and maintains spot plates. The output intent carries the profile; per X-1a, individual profiles are not embedded.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B is tempting because the document CMYK is set, but it leaves RGB unconverted, violating X-1a and causing device-dependent color. C converts everything including CMYK, which alters carefully specified CMYK numbers and can break TAC. D converts toward sRGB, which is wrong for press-bound PDFs.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You exported an A4 flyer; the printer reports faint white slivers along the trim on a background photo that touches the edge. Your export settings were:
```text
Marks & Bleeds:
  Crop Marks: ON
  Bleed: Top 0 mm, Bottom 0 mm, Inside 0 mm, Outside 0 mm
Document:
  Background image extends exactly to the page edge
``` 
What minimal change prevents the hairlines without scaling the whole layout?
options:
```text
Add a 3 mm Slug area and keep content inside the slug.
```

```text
Set Bleed to 3 mm on all sides; extend background beyond trim to the bleed; re-export with crop marks and bleed.
```

```text
Leave Bleed at 0 mm; turn ON Registration Marks to improve cutter alignment.
```

```text
Scale the entire document to 101% on export so the image exceeds the page.
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: Hairlines from trim variance are prevented by adding bleed and extending artwork past trim. Crop/registration marks cannot compensate for missing bleed. Scaling everything risks margin and type safety.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B sounds like precision will fix it, but registration marks don’t replace bleed. C seems like a shortcut but distorts layout and safe areas. D confuses slug (notes space) with bleed (ink beyond trim).

concept_mcqs.stem:
Preflight flags small body copy set to a rich black swatch in your brochure:
```text
Swatch: Rich Black
Values: C60 M40 Y40 K100
Usage: Paragraph style 'Body-7pt', Fill = Rich Black, Overprint Fill = OFF
Issue: Potential registration/halo risk for small text
``` 
What is the correct fix for the body text?
options:
```text
Outline the text to convert it to vector paths at the same rich black values.
```

```text
Apply 'Registration' color so all plates align perfectly.
```

```text
Keep rich black but set Overprint Fill = ON so plates don’t knock out.
```

```text
Change body text fill to K=100 only and set Overprint Fill = ON.
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: Small text should be 100% K only to avoid registration issues. Overprinting 100K text prevents tiny knockouts that can cause halos. Rich black is reserved for large areas, not fine text.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B assumes overprint alone fixes registration; it still prints on four plates and risks fuzziness. C “Registration” color prints on all plates at 100% and is for marks only—catastrophic in content. D outlining doesn’t fix multi-plate misregistration from rich black.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Your preflight reports excessive total ink in a hero panel:
```text
Sampled pixel: C=85 M=75 Y=70 K=85  (TAC = 315%)
Printer spec: ISO Coated v2 300% (ECI), Max TAC = 300%
Document: Mixed RGB and CMYK assets
``` 
Which export strategy best ensures all content meets TAC without manual recoloring per object?
options:
```text
Output: Convert to Destination (not Preserve Numbers)
Destination: ISO Coated v2 300% (ECI)
```

```text
Convert everything to sRGB first, then back to CMYK ISO Coated v2.
```

```text
Leave conversion OFF and ask the printer’s RIP to enforce TAC.
```

```text
Reduce K by -15% with a Curves adjustment layer on the CMYK hero image only, leave other assets unchanged.
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: Converting all colors to a 300% TAC profile ensures both RGB and existing CMYK tones are remapped to respect ink limits. Preserve Numbers must be off so existing CMYK is converted too.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B may fix one image but misses other assets and is manual-error-prone. C double-conversion increases gamut loss and artifacts. D offloads color to the RIP, risking unpredictable remapping and contract color issues.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Your layout uses drop shadows over a spot varnish plate and a die-line. The printer’s RIP supports PDF 1.6. With your current PDF/X-1a export, they report transparency flattened around spot areas, creating unwanted process conversions.

Which export choice preserves spot plates and live transparency?
options:
```text
Export: PDF/X-3:2002
Output: Convert to Destination
```

```text
Export: High Quality Print (no standard)
Output: No Color Conversion
```

```text
Export: PDF/X-4:2010
Output: Convert to Destination (Preserve Numbers)
Ink Manager: All Spots to Process = OFF
```

```text
Export: PDF/X-1a:2001
Transparency Flattener: High Resolution
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: PDF/X-4 maintains live transparency and keeps spot colors as separate plates when All Spots to Process is off. With a modern RIP, this avoids flattening artifacts around spot objects.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B flattens transparency by definition in X-1a, increasing risk of spot-to-process in blend regions. C is unmanaged and may leave RGB or device-dependent color. D X-3 allows profiles but still flattens transparency and is less suitable for spot+transparency workflows.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Your placed brand logo is an Illustrator file containing live text set in a licensed font you cannot redistribute. InDesign preflight shows:
```text
Links: brand_logo.ai — Font 'Gotham Book' MISSING in linked asset
Requirement: Printer must receive a file with no missing fonts and identical appearance.
``` 
What is the safest fix?
options:
```text
Allow InDesign to substitute a similar system font in the placed AI file.
```

```text
Open brand_logo.ai, convert the logo text to outlines, save, relink, and re-export PDF.
```

```text
Package and send the Gotham font to the printer despite licensing.
```

```text
Rasterize the entire page at 300 ppi before export to avoid font issues.
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: Outlining the logo text resolves the missing-font dependency without changing appearance and avoids licensing violations. It localizes the change to the logo asset rather than rasterizing whole pages.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B will reflow/change metrics. C destroys vector quality and increases file size. D violates licensing and may expose you legally.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You are producing a true 2-spot poster (Pantone 286 C and Pantone 877 C). A last-minute issue appears in the PDF output preview:
```text
Ink Manager:
  All Spots to Process: ON
Separations Preview:
  Plates: C, M, Y, K only; no spot plates present
``` 
How do you fix this to deliver a 2-spot job?
options:
```text
Turn OFF 'All Spots to Process' and ensure both Pantone swatches are defined as Spot, then re-export (PDF/X-1a or X-4).
```

```text
Leave as is and request the printer to re-separate the PDF back to spot plates.
```

```text
Change both Pantone swatches to Process and increase saturation by +20%.
```

```text
Convert the document to Grayscale and tint to simulate the two inks.
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: With All Spots to Process off and swatches defined as Spot, the exported PDF will carry separate spot plates for a 2-ink job.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B turns it into CMYK, not a 2-spot job. C re-separation from process to spot is unreliable and not the printer’s responsibility. D grayscale cannot represent metallic or specific Pantone hues as discrete plates.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Your preflight flags an image as low-res, but the report shows:
```text
Link: hero_photo.jpg
Actual PPI: 150
Scaling: 50%
Effective PPI: 300
Preflight Rule: Raster images below 250 PPI — based on Actual PPI
Status: ERROR
``` 
What is the correct remedy?
options:
```text
Ignore the error; all low-res warnings are false positives.
```

```text
Change the preflight rule to evaluate Effective PPI instead of Actual PPI; no resampling needed.
```

```text
Upsample the file in Photoshop to 300 PPI at 100% and relink.
```

```text
Scale the placed image to 100% to match Actual and Effective PPI.
```
concept_mcqs.explanation: Print sharpness depends on effective PPI at the placed scale. The image is effectively 300 PPI; the rule must reference effective PPI to avoid false errors.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B wastes time and can degrade quality. C breaks the layout. D dismisses genuine warnings; only this one is misconfigured.

concept_mcqs.stem: You sent the client a CMYK PDF proof of a poster. They view it in a non–color-managed viewer on Windows and say the colors look dull. Production requires PDF/X for print. What proofing workflow minimizes approval friction while keeping production color intact?
options: Embed the monitor ICC profile into the PDF/X file so it matches the client’s screen.
Only send the PDF/X file and ask the client to install and use Adobe Acrobat with Output Preview.
Convert the entire project to sRGB so the PDF looks vibrant on all screens, then reconvert to CMYK before print.
Provide two deliverables: on-screen proofs as sRGB JPEG/PNG exports (from a CMYK soft-proofed view) for client approval, and a separate PDF/X print file for production.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Clients typically use unmanaged viewers. Screen-proof in sRGB for approvals and supply a separate, color-managed PDF/X for print. This avoids reconversion while aligning expectations.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B is fragile and adds friction; they may still not view it correctly. C round-trips color and risks shifts. D embedding a monitor profile in PDF/X is inappropriate and doesn’t control the client’s viewer behavior.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You are assembling a case-study deck for the capstone. Which slide order best tells a coherent story from brief to outcome while signaling print-production readiness?

Option A:
```text
1 Final visuals
2 Concepts A/B
3 Brief & constraints
4 Iterations
5 Production specs
6 Outcomes & reflection
```

Option B:
```text
1 Brief & constraints
2 Success metrics
3 Concepts A/B with rationale
4 Iterations responding to feedback
5 Final visuals (print + mockups)
6 Production specs (profiles, TAC, bleed)
7 Outcomes & reflection
```

Option C:
```text
1 Moodboards
2 Process photos
3 Final visuals
4 Iterations
5 Outcomes
6 Production specs
```

Option D:
```text
1 Final visuals
2 Outcomes
3 Production specs
4 Concepts
5 Brief
6 Iterations
```
options: B
D
A
C
concept_mcqs.explanation: B leads with the brief and constraints, sets success criteria, shows concept rationale, then iteration, then finals and production readiness, and ends with outcomes and reflection. It matches how stakeholders process decisions and reduces cognitive load.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A starts with the answer, hiding the why. C emphasizes mood/process ephemera over decision-making and production. D back-loads context, forcing the audience to reframe midstream.

scenario_questions.scenario: You’re delivering a folding carton artwork that includes: a magenta die-line, a spot gloss varnish (named VARNISH), CMYK artwork with transparent drop shadows, and placed logos with spot Pantone colors. The printer confirms their RIP supports PDF 1.6 and requests separate plates for die and varnish, no unintended knockouts, and no transparency flattening artifacts. Your last PDF/X-1a was rejected for flattening near spot objects and knockouts under varnish.
scenario_questions.task: Describe precisely how you will adjust the document setup and export to meet the printer’s requirements. Include: swatch definitions and attributes (overprint/knockout), layer/visibility guidance for proof vs production, Ink Manager settings, appropriate PDF standard and Output settings, and how you will verify plates before delivery. Justify each decision in terms of prepress risks you’re avoiding.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
- Keep die-line and varnish as distinct Spot swatches (e.g., DIE, VARNISH), 100% tints only; set both to Overprint Stroke/Fill so they do not create knockouts in CMYK artwork. Place them on their own top layers. For the die-line, either supply two PDFs (production with DIE layer hidden; proof with DIE visible) or keep DIE visible but confirm the printer treats the plate as technical (non-printing) if requested.
- Ensure Pantone brand colors remain defined as Spot and avoid inadvertently converting them in Ink Manager (All Spots to Process = OFF).
- Export as PDF/X-4 to preserve live transparency; set Output to Convert to Destination (Preserve Numbers) with the printer’s CMYK profile as Output Intent. If a TAC-limited profile is specified, ensure all colors, including existing CMYK, are compliant (optionally use Convert to Destination without Preserve Numbers if the printer requests remapping to a TAC-limited profile).
- Verify plates in Acrobat Output Preview: confirm separate spot plates for DIE and VARNISH, spot Pantones intact, no unexpected CMYK builds where spots should be. Toggle Overprint Preview ON to ensure no knockouts appear beneath VARNISH.
- Re-preflight the PDF: no RGB, effective resolution sufficient, fonts embedded, bleed present per dieline perimeter. Document the checks in a preflight report for the printer.

rubric.criterion: Correct spot color setup (distinct Spot swatches for DIE and VARNISH, 100% tints, overprint attributes)
Appropriate PDF standard and output strategy (PDF/X-4, correct Output Intent, rationale re: transparency)
Ink Manager and plate preservation (spots not forced to process; Pantones retained)
Verification steps (Acrobat Output Preview with Overprint Preview; preflight checks; bleed)
Justification tied to avoiding knockouts/flattening artifacts and TAC non-compliance

scenario_questions.scenario:
Capstone brief excerpt:
```text
Client: City Arts Fest
Deliverable: A3 poster (297×420 mm), print run 5,000, uncoated stock
Brand colors: Pantone 1655 C (primary), Black
Constraints: Budget allows 2-color spot or 4-color CMYK; decision pending
Feedback after Concept Round 1:
  - Stakeholder A: "Make the orange neon and more saturated"
  - Stakeholder B: "Type feels tight near margins"
  - Production partner: "Uncoated stock will dull chroma; recommend spot match or CMYK with GCR, TAC ≤ 300%"
Timeline: 1 week, 2 review rounds max
```
scenario_questions.task: Propose an iteration plan for Round 2 that addresses feedback and production constraints. State which feedback to adopt or push back on, your color route recommendation (2-spot vs CMYK) with reasoning for uncoated stock, specific layout adjustments, proofing approach for stakeholder approvals, and what you will present in the meeting to keep decisions focused.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
- Adopt B’s margin feedback: increase margins or adjust the grid to improve breathing room and avoid trim risk; show margin-safe guides in proofs.
- Push back on A’s “neon” ask: explain uncoated stock and print gamut limits; propose either (1) a 2-spot route using Pantone 1655 U (uncoated formulation) plus Black, or (2) a CMYK route tuned for uncoated (ISO Uncoated profile), ensuring TAC ≤ 300% and robust GCR to stabilize neutrals.
- Recommendation: If brand fidelity to orange is critical, choose 2-spot using 1655 U to minimize dulling; otherwise CMYK route with proofs showing expected shift on uncoated.
- Proofing: Provide on-screen sRGB proofs for stakeholder review and a contract-quality print proof or a calibrated soft-proof PDF with Output Preview instructions; include side-by-side swatches comparing coated vs uncoated appearance.
- Meeting artifacts: a one-page decision matrix (2-spot vs CMYK trade-offs: cost, fidelity, schedule), updated layouts with adjusted margins, and a color rendering comparison. Lock route by meeting end to preserve the two-round limit.

rubric.criterion: Clear accept/push-back mapping of feedback with rationale tied to constraints
Color route recommendation justified for uncoated stock (Pantone U vs CMYK with profile/GCR/TAC)
Concrete layout adjustments addressing margins/trim safety
Proofing/approval plan suitable for stakeholders and production (on-screen + print/soft-proof)
Meeting artifacts that focus decisions and control rounds/scope

scenario_questions.scenario: You’re preparing a 2×3 m outdoor billboard viewed from ~10 m. Source images are 72 ppi at full size. The printer requests PDF/X-4 with a CMYK profile capped at TAC 260% and warns against heavy small-type overprints.
scenario_questions.task: Decide whether the imagery resolution is acceptable and how to structure the file for output. Specify your working scale (if any), target effective PPI at that scale, handling of small text/linework, and any color/TAC conversion steps. Justify in terms of viewing distance, RIP behavior, and risk areas.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
- For large-format at 10 m, effective 30–100 ppi at final size is typically acceptable; 72 ppi at full size is fine for imagery. Alternatively, work at 25% scale with images at ~288 ppi effective to keep links manageable, but note that effective PPI at final remains ~72 ppi.
- Keep vector logos/type as vector; avoid rich black small text and avoid overprinting fine type on varied backgrounds—use 100K for small copy and ensure legibility given distance.
- Export PDF/X-4 to keep live transparency; set Output to Convert to Destination (not Preserve Numbers if needed) with the 260% TAC profile so all assets respect ink limits.
- Preflight to ensure no unintended hairlines at panel seams and adequate bleed/overlap per vendor’s spec; check scaling so stroke weights aren’t too thin at final size.

rubric.criterion: Resolution judgment tied to viewing distance and effective PPI reasoning
Appropriate scale strategy and implications for vectors/strokes/type
Color/TAC conversion choice consistent with vendor spec and X-4
Risk mitigation: overprint/text handling, seams/bleed checks

scenario_questions.scenario: You’re turning your capstone into a case-study portfolio entry. You have: the original brief PDF, two divergent concept boards, annotated iteration screenshots, a final print-ready PDF, and printer feedback emails that led to changes (bleed increase, TAC limit). You have no permission to share sales figures.
scenario_questions.task: Outline exactly how you will structure the case-study and what artifacts you will include on each page to demonstrate process rigor and production readiness without revealing confidential results. Include how you’ll present outcomes credibly, design the deck for screen viewing, and reference production decisions succinctly during a live presentation.
scenario_questions.expected_answer:
- Structure: 1) Brief & constraints (screenshot highlights, goals, audience); 2) Success criteria (qualitative proxies); 3) Concepts A/B with rationale and intended trade-offs; 4) Iteration timeline with side-by-side before/after callouts tied to feedback emails; 5) Final visuals (print and in-situ mockups); 6) Production spec sheet (profiles, PDF/X, bleed, TAC, spot usage) in a compact panel; 7) Outcomes & reflection using non-confidential proxies (e.g., qualitative feedback, print quality improvements, on-time delivery), plus next-steps.
- Outcomes: Use proxy metrics (e.g., “approved in 2 rounds vs planned 2”, on-press match within ΔE threshold if available, stakeholder quotes) rather than sales.
- Screen design: export an sRGB PDF with type ≥14 pt, consistent grid and typography, and compressed images; provide a separate print appendix if needed.
- Live presentation cues: narrate decisions-to-constraints mapping, flag production checkpoints (preflight pass, output intent, plate checks) in one slide to show diligence without overwhelming detail.

rubric.criterion: Clear narrative structure linking brief → concepts → iteration → final → production → outcomes
Appropriate use of artifacts (screenshots, before/after, proof specs) that evidence rigor
Ethical outcome presentation using credible proxies, not confidential data
Screen-first presentation craft and readiness for live delivery
Concise production-readiness communication (profiles, PDF/X, bleed, TAC)

practical_tasks.title: Produce a print-ready A4 flyer with spot varnish (print-ready artwork)
practical_tasks.brief: Create a two-sided A4 flyer for a fictional product. Include a photographic background, vector branding, body copy, and a selective spot gloss varnish on key elements. Printer requirements: PDF/X-4, ISO Coated v2 300% (ECI) output intent, 3 mm bleed, crop marks, max TAC 300%, minimum text size 6 pt for body, preserve spot plates. practical_tasks.title: Capstone case-study portfolio (6–10 pages, screen-first)
